skill.name: azure-communication-chat-java
skill.description: Build Java chat features with Azure Communication Services, including threads, messages, participants, read receipts, and typing notifications.
skill.summary: Java guidance for Azure Communication Services chat workflows and SDK usage.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Static command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline API names. The Azure endpoint values are placeholders for expected SDK configuration. Contextual review found low to medium application risks around logging chat data and handling HTML chat messages.

remediation.issue: Console output examples include chat content, participant identifiers, and read-receipt identifiers.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to avoid logging message bodies, user identifiers, and read receipts in production. Use redaction for troubleshooting logs.

remediation.issue: HTML chat message examples do not mention sanitization.
remediation.suggestion: Warn developers to sanitize or reject user-supplied HTML before sending or rendering chat messages.

remediation.issue: Token placeholders appear in setup examples without storage guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to store tokens securely, avoid committing them, and use short-lived tokens with refresh logic.

semantic_findings.title: Chat Data Printed to Console
semantic_findings.description: Examples print message content, participant identifiers, and read-receipt senders. If copied into production logging, chat content and identifiers could be exposed.

semantic_findings.title: HTML Message Sanitization Guidance Missing
semantic_findings.description: The skill demonstrates sending HTML chat messages without warning about sanitizing user-supplied HTML. Rendered chat clients could introduce cross-site scripting.

content.value_statement: Java teams need clear examples for Azure Communication Services chat. This skill shows thread, message, participant, receipt, and typing workflows.
actual_capabilities: Shows Maven dependency setup for the Azure Communication Chat Java SDK.
Creates synchronous and asynchronous chat clients with token credentials.
Creates chat threads and adds named participants.
Sends, lists, updates, and deletes chat messages.
Manages participants, read receipts, typing notifications, and thread properties.
Demonstrates pagination, environment variables, and basic HTTP error handling.
limitations: It provides examples, not a complete production application.
It does not generate Azure resources or issue user access tokens.
It does not cover client UI rendering or message storage design.
Security controls need project-specific validation before deployment.

use_cases.title: Add Chat to a Java App
use_cases.description: Use the examples to wire Azure chat clients, threads, and message operations into an existing Java service.

use_cases.title: Prototype Team Messaging
use_cases.description: Create a working proof of concept with participants, read receipts, and typing notifications.

use_cases.title: Review SDK Workflows
use_cases.description: Map required Azure Communication Services chat calls before writing implementation tickets or integration tests.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Chat Client
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a Java service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to show the Maven dependency and Java code for creating an Azure Communication Services chat client.

prompt_templates.title: Build Thread Messaging
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design Java code for creating a chat thread, adding participants, sending messages, and listing messages.

prompt_templates.title: Add Chat Interaction Features
prompt_templates.scenario: Extend a chat feature with user signals.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add read receipts, typing notifications, participant management, and pagination to a Java chat workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Production Integration
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare implementation guidance for a team.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a production-ready Azure chat integration plan, including error handling, token refresh, pagination, and security checks.

output_examples.input: Create a Java flow for a new project chat thread with two users.
output_examples.output: A concise implementation outline with dependency setup, credential creation, participant creation, thread creation, and thread client retrieval.

output_examples.input: Add read receipts and typing notifications to an existing Java chat feature.
output_examples.output: A focused checklist covering SDK calls, expected inputs, user interface triggers, and validation points for receipt and typing behavior.

output_examples.input: Review the risks before using HTML chat messages.
output_examples.output: Security guidance that recommends sanitizing user-provided HTML, limiting allowed tags, and testing how clients render message content.

best_practices: Use short-lived user tokens and implement refresh logic before launch.
Paginate message and thread lists to avoid slow or memory-heavy responses.
Redact message bodies, user identifiers, and receipt data from production logs.
anti_patterns: Do not commit user access tokens or resource endpoints into source control.
Do not render user-supplied HTML chat content without sanitization.
Do not share full thread history with new participants unless the product requires it.

faq.question: Does this skill create Azure resources?
faq.answer: No. It assumes an Azure Communication Services resource and valid user access tokens already exist.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it include asynchronous Java examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how to build an asynchronous chat client with the Azure SDK.

faq.question: Does it cover participant management?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes listing, adding, and removing participants from a chat thread.

faq.question: What security checks should I add?
faq.answer: Protect tokens, sanitize HTML message content, limit shared history, and avoid logging private chat data.

faq.question: Is this a complete application template?
faq.answer: No. It is reference guidance for SDK workflows and still needs project-specific code, testing, and deployment work.
